s1.title: PMO Setup & Structuring

s2.title: PMO & Project Management

about.title: About me
about.p1: I'm Renato Decker. I've spent over 20 years managing projects in environments where stopping is not an option — 24/7 industrial operations, teams of up to 20 people, complex system integrations, and clients at vastly different levels of maturity.
about.p2: I'm not the consultant who delivers a methodology deck and disappears. I stay through go-live. I adjust the plan when scope changes in week five. I negotiate between stakeholders with conflicting goals. And I make knowledge transfer real — to the client, to their team, to whoever will keep the system running.
about.p3: Method matters. But what actually delivers results is pragmatism, adaptability, and an unrelenting focus on what truly matters to the business.

symptoms.title: Do any of these sound familiar?
symptoms.subtitle: If so, you're in the right place.
symptoms.s1: Projects that keep slipping — despite schedules, weekly check-ins, and everyone's best intentions
symptoms.s2: Executive management without real visibility: reports exist, but nobody trusts the numbers
symptoms.s3: Dozens of initiatives competing for the same resources with no clear prioritization
symptoms.s4: A PMO that generates artifacts and reports but removes no obstacles and makes no decisions
symptoms.s5: Project managers with solid training who freeze under pressure, conflict, and organizational politics
symptoms.s6: Scope that changes constantly, with no one having clear authority to decide

c1.challenge: Implementation in an industrial slaughterhouse running 24/7 — zero tolerance for downtime. Integration of shop floor, WMS, shipping, and quality with existing production systems. Scope under constant adjustment due to client-required customizations.
c1.result: Delivered on time. 20% reduction in data entry rework. Integrated inventory and shipping with real-time visibility across the entire operation.

c2.challenge: Integration of an ERP — with heavily customized commercial policies — into a B2B platform built by a third party. No prior experience with this type of integration. Client's online processes undefined at project start.
c2.result: After three distinct technical approaches, a hybrid sync/async model was built from scratch. Go-live completed with full data integrity and commercial policies working correctly online.

c3.challenge: Full back-office and production implementation with a client team smaller than typical for this scale. All training was directed to a third-party consulting firm contracted by the client to operate the system — no qualified internal team to receive knowledge directly.
c3.result: Delivered on time and within budget. Consulting firm fully trained to operate all modules and provide independent support to the client.

summary.title: About
summary.p1: Over 20 years delivering high-complexity projects in critical industrial environments — 24/7 operations where a system failure means a production halt. Managing cross-functional teams of up to 20 professionals: developers, business analysts, and implementation consultants in the field.
summary.p2: Specialist across the full project lifecycle: from diagnosis to go-live and knowledge transfer. Deep experience in multi-module ERP implementations, integrations between disparate platforms, scope management under constant change, and navigating multiple stakeholders — client, vendors, and internal teams. When plan A doesn't work, plan B is already being built.
summary.p3: Every project brings a different problem: small client teams, tight budgets, unprecedented integrations, scope that changes the week of go-live. The method matters — but what delivers results is knowing how to adapt, decide under pressure, and get the team across the finish line within whatever constraints the context allows.

r1.title: Implementation Manager
r1.desc: Managed the Implementation area with 6 PMs and 20 consultants, portfolio of ~45 active projects — 20+ implementations for new clients and 40+ for existing ones. Projects across all regions of Brazil and Latin America (Paraguay and Peru). Redesigned the implementation methodology, reducing costs and delivery time, and developed project managers.

r2.title: Product Manager
r2.desc: Led a team of 14 analysts and developers. Implemented agile methods, product roadmap and backlog management. Strategic alignment between business and technology areas, portfolio prioritization, and delivery management.

r3.title: Software Development Portfolio Manager
r3.desc: Supported the PM team by removing obstacles and negotiating priorities, resources, and deadlines between development and business. Created the company's project office, establishing the project management methodology that structures the area to this day.

r4.title: Support & Service Manager
r4.desc: Managed level-1 support (6 people) and level-2 support (14 people). Defined and controlled SLAs, implemented quality KPIs, escalation processes, and continuous improvement initiatives.

r5.title: Project Manager
r5.desc: Requirements analysis, feasibility studies, and project planning. Development coordination, deadline control, and compliance with requirements. On-site follow-up during implementations, ensuring correct functioning of the delivered product.

r6.title: Tech Lead
r6.desc: Technical lead for PCP, Shop Floor, Inventory, WMS, and Logistics products. Led a team of 4, monitored performance, and distributed tasks. Development in Progress OpenEdge.

r7.title: Systems Analyst / Software Developer
r7.desc: Analysis and development of PCP, Shop Floor, Inventory, WMS, and Logistics products in Progress OpenEdge. The technical foundation that underpinned the career path into project management and product ownership.
